topics.title: Introduction, Statutory Requirement & Meaning of E-Way Bill
explain: Under GST, physical boundary check-posts are abolished to ensure free movement of goods.
To prevent tax evasion, Section 68 mandates carrying prescribed documents during transit.
An E-Way Bill (Form GST EWB-01) is an electronic document generated on the GST portal evidencing movement of goods.
Information must be uploaded on the common portal (www.ewaybillgst.gov.in) prior to movement.
Provisions of CGST Act regarding E-Way Bill apply equally to IGST Act under Section 20.

flow.title: E-Way Bill Generation Workflow
steps: Upload transaction details on GST portal
Generate Part-A slip with temporary number
Enter vehicle/transport details in Part-B
System generates unique E-Way Bill Number
Carry E-Way Bill during movement of goods

topics.example: A supplier in Punjab wants to send goods to Gujarat. Before loading the truck, the supplier logs onto the E-Way Bill portal and inputs transaction details to obtain the electronic waybill.
remember: Website for E-Way Bill: www.ewaybillgst.gov.in
E-Way Bill provisions are contained in Rule 138 of CGST Rules, 2017.
mistakes: Thinking E-Way Bill is required for movement of services. It applies strictly to goods.

quiz.q: Which section of the CGST Act mandates carrying documents during movement of goods?
quiz.why: Section 68 of the CGST Act stipulates that the person in charge of a conveyance carrying goods must carry prescribed documents.

quiz.q: What is an E-Way Bill?
o: A physical paper tax invoice issued by the buyer
An electronic document generated on the GST portal evidencing movement of goods
A state border entry permit issued by police
A certificate of origin issued by customs
quiz.why: E-Way Bill is a digital interface document generated on the GST portal prior to commencement of movement of goods.

topics.title: Consignment Value & Mandatory Generation Cases
explain: E-Way Bill is mandatory when consignment value of goods exceeds ₹ 50,000.
It is required for supply, reasons other than supply, or inward supply from an unregistered person.
Consignment value is determined under Section 15 and declared in invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan.
It includes GST (CGST, SGST, IGST, Cess) charged in the document.
It excludes the value of exempt supply if invoice is issued for both exempt and taxable supplies.
Mandatory generation applies even if value is ≤ ₹ 50,000 for inter-State transfer of handicraft goods by persons exempted from registration.

flow.title: Determining Consignment Value for E-Way Bill
steps: Take taxable value under Section 15
Add GST taxes and Cess charged
Exclude exempt goods value (if joint invoice)
Check if total exceeds ₹ 50,000 limit
Generate E-Way Bill if limit crossed

topics.example: Bhanupratap sold shoes for ₹ 48,000 (excluding 18% GST). Consignment value = ₹ 48,000 × 118% = ₹ 56,640. Since ₹ 56,640 > ₹ 50,000, E-Way Bill is mandatory.
remember: Threshold limit: Consignment value exceeding ₹ 50,000.
Handicraft goods inter-State movement requires E-Way Bill irrespective of consignment value.
mistakes: Calculating the threshold limit of ₹ 50,000 without including GST taxes.
Including exempt goods value when a single invoice covers both exempt and taxable goods.

quiz.q: What is the monetary threshold for mandatory E-Way Bill generation?
quiz.why: Rule 138(1) requires an E-Way Bill whenever movement of goods has a consignment value exceeding ₹ 50,000.

quiz.q: In which scenario must an E-Way Bill be generated even if consignment value is less than ₹ 50,000?
o: Inter-State transfer of handicraft goods by a person exempt from registration
Transportation of petrol by tank lorry
quiz.why: As per 4th proviso to Rule 138(1), inter-State transport of handicraft goods by exempt persons requires E-Way Bill regardless of value.

topics.title: E-Way Bill in 'Bill To Ship To' Model
explain: In a 'Bill To Ship To' model, person A orders supplier B to ship goods directly to recipient C.
This transaction involves two supplies and two tax invoices (Invoice 1: B to A; Invoice 2: A to C).
Although two invoices are issued, physical movement of goods takes place directly from B to C.
Only ONE E-Way Bill is required for the entire movement of goods.
Either person A or supplier B can generate the single E-Way Bill.

flow.title: 'Bill To Ship To' E-Way Bill Process
steps: A places order to B to send goods to C
B issues Invoice-1 to A
A issues Invoice-2 to C
Either A or B generates ONE E-Way Bill
Goods physically move from B directly to C

topics.example: Ashok (Delhi) asks Bhagwati (Jaipur) to deliver goods directly to Chandra (Lucknow). Two invoices are generated, but only one E-Way Bill is created by either Ashok or Bhagwati for movement from Jaipur to Lucknow.
remember: Two invoices are generated in Bill-to-Ship-to model.
Only ONE E-Way Bill is required for the entire physical movement.
mistakes: Generating two separate E-Way Bills for the single physical movement in a Bill-to-Ship-to transaction.

quiz.q: How many E-Way Bills are required in a 'Bill To Ship To' supply model for one physical movement?
quiz.why: Press Release dated 23.04.2018 clarifies that only one E-Way Bill is required for the physical movement from supplier to recipient.

quiz.q: Who among the following can generate the E-Way Bill in a 'Bill To Ship To' transaction?
o: Either buyer A or supplier B
quiz.why: Either person A (who ordered the goods) or supplier B (who ships the goods) can generate the single E-Way Bill.

topics.title: Information to be Furnished in Form GST EWB-01 (Part A & Part B)
explain: Form GST EWB-01 consists of two distinct parts: Part A and Part B.
Part A contains GSTIN of supplier & recipient, place of delivery (PIN code), document details, value of goods, HSN code, and reason for transport.
Part A is furnished by the registered person causing movement of goods.
Part B contains transport details (vehicle number for road, or GRN/RR/Airway Bill/Bill of Lading number).
Part B is furnished by the person transporting the goods.
E-Way Bill becomes valid for movement by road ONLY after Part B details are entered.

flow.title: Form GST EWB-01 Completion Flow
steps: Fill Part A with invoice & HSN details
Generate temporary Part A slip
Enter vehicle / transport document in Part B
Complete E-Way Bill generation
E-Way Bill becomes valid for movement

topics.example: A seller creates Part A using the invoice details and gets a temporary slip. Once the truck arrives, the vehicle number is entered into Part B to complete and activate the E-Way Bill.
remember: Part A = Consignment details (Invoice, HSN, Value, PIN).
Part B = Transport details (Vehicle No / Document No).
E-Way Bill is valid for road movement only when Part B is filled.
mistakes: Believing that generating Part A slip alone allows commencement of road transportation without filling Part B.

quiz.q: Which part of Form GST EWB-01 contains the vehicle number for road transport?
quiz.why: Part B of Form GST EWB-01 is dedicated to transport details such as vehicle number or transport document number.

quiz.q: Who primarily furnishes the information in Part A of Form GST EWB-01?
o: The registered person causing movement of goods
quiz.why: Part A details are to be furnished by the registered person causing the movement of goods (consignor/consignee).

topics.title: Responsibility to Generate E-Way Bill & Transporter Roles
explain: If registered consignor/consignee transports in own/hired conveyance, they must fill Part B and generate E-Way Bill [Rule 138(2)].
If goods are handed over to a road transporter without E-Way Bill, registered person inputs Part A and transporter generates E-Way Bill by filling Part B [Rule 138(3)].
For transport by railways/air/vessel, registered supplier or recipient must generate E-Way Bill [Rule 138(2A)].
Railways will not deliver goods unless E-Way Bill is produced at the time of delivery.
Unregistered transporters must register on the EWB portal to get a 15-digit unique TRANSIN id.
E-Way Bill can be re-assigned to another transporter for completing transport via Part B update [Rule 138(5A)].

flow.title: Transporter Re-assignment Flow
steps: Consignor inputs Part A details
Consignor assigns EWB to Transporter A
Transporter A moves goods to intermediate location
Transporter A re-assigns EWB to Transporter B
Transporter B updates Part B and completes delivery

topics.example: A seller sends goods via Transporter A from City X to City Y. For the leg from City Y to City Z, Transporter A re-assigns the E-Way Bill to Transporter B, who updates vehicle details in Part B.
remember: TRANSIN = 15-digit Unique Transporter ID for unregistered transporters.
Railways require E-Way Bill produced at delivery, not during transit.
Once Part B is updated by transporter, consignor cannot reassign EWB to another transporter.
mistakes: Assuming railways carry physical copy of E-Way Bill during train movement.

quiz.q: What is the 15-digit unique ID issued to an unregistered transporter on the E-Way Bill portal called?
quiz.why: Unregistered transporters get a 15-digit Unique Transporter ID called TRANSIN upon enrolling on the EWB portal.

quiz.q: When must an E-Way Bill be produced in case of transport of goods by Railways?
o: At the time of loading the train
At the time of delivery of goods
quiz.why: Proviso to Rule 138(2A) states that railways shall deliver goods only when the E-Way Bill is produced at the time of delivery.

topics.title: Conveyance Part-B Exceptions & Transshipment Rules
explain: Exception to Part-B: Vehicle details in Part-B are NOT mandatory if distance is up to 50 km within same State/UT.
This exception applies from consignor's place to transporter's place, or from transporter's place to consignee's place.
If goods are transferred from one conveyance to another in transit (transshipment), Part B vehicle details must be updated on portal before transfer.
Vehicle number can be updated in Part-B multiple times within the overall validity period.
The latest vehicle number on the E-Way Bill must match the physical vehicle carrying the goods.

flow.title: Transshipment Vehicle Updation Process
steps: Vehicle A breaks down or transshipment needed
Log into E-Way Bill portal prior to movement
Select 'Update Vehicle Number' option
Enter new Vehicle B details in Part-B
Resume transit with updated E-Way Bill

topics.example: A factory sends goods 30 km to a local transporter's godown within Maharashtra. Part B vehicle details are not mandatory for this 30 km intra-state leg.
remember: 50 km distance limit within same State/UT for Part-B exemption.
Must update Part-B prior to moving goods in new vehicle during transshipment.
mistakes: Applying the 50 km Part-B exemption for inter-State movements.

quiz.q: Part-B vehicle details are optional for transport within the same State up to what distance?
quiz.why: Third proviso to Rule 138(3) exempts Part-B details for distances up to 50 km within the same State/UT between business place and transporter.

quiz.q: When a truck carrying goods breaks down and goods are shifted to a new truck, what must be done?
o: Update vehicle details in Part B of E-Way Bill prior to further movement
Cancel the existing E-Way Bill and issue a new one
No action required if within same city
quiz.why: Under Rule 138(5), when goods are transferred to another conveyance, transporter/consignor must update Part B before further movement.

topics.title: Consolidated E-Way Bill
explain: Consolidated E-Way Bill (Form GST EWB-02) is generated when multiple consignments are transported in a single conveyance.
The transporter indicates serial numbers of individual E-Way Bills on the portal to generate Form GST EWB-02.
It acts like a trip sheet for the transporter carrying goods from multiple consignors/consignees.
Consolidated E-Way Bill has NO independent validity period; each consignment relies on its own individual EWB validity.
Generation of Form GST EWB-02 is optional, not mandatory.
Multiple invoices of the same consignor/consignee cannot be clubbed into one individual EWB, but individual EWBs can be consolidated in EWB-02.

flow.title: Consolidated E-Way Bill Generation
steps: Collect multiple consignments with individual EWBs
Log in to E-Way Bill portal as transporter
Select individual E-Way Bill numbers
System generates Form GST EWB-02
Carry single Consolidated EWB in vehicle

topics.example: A logistics operator loads 5 different shipments (each having its own EWB) into one truck. Instead of holding 5 separate papers, he generates one Consolidated E-Way Bill (Form GST EWB-02).
remember: Form GST EWB-02 = Consolidated E-Way Bill.
It is optional and has NO independent validity period.
mistakes: Clubbing multiple invoices into one EWB-01 instead of generating separate EWB-01 for each invoice.

quiz.q: Which form is used for generating a Consolidated E-Way Bill?
quiz.why: Rule 138(6) prescribes Form GST EWB-02 for generating a consolidated E-Way Bill.

quiz.q: What is the validity period of a Consolidated E-Way Bill?
o: It has no independent validity period
Same as the shortest distance EWB
quiz.why: Consolidated EWB does not have an independent validity period; individual consignments must reach their destination within their respective EWB validity.

topics.title: Cancellation & Validity Period of E-Way Bill
explain: Cancellation: An E-Way Bill can be cancelled electronically within 24 hours of generation if goods are not transported or details are wrong.
Cancellation is barred if the E-Way Bill has been verified in transit under Rule 138B.
Unique EWB number generated is valid for 15 days for Part B updation.
Validity Calculation (Normal Cargo): Up to 200 km = 1 day; every additional 200 km or part thereof = 1 additional day.
Validity Calculation (Over Dimensional Cargo / Ship Multimodal): Up to 20 km = 1 day; every additional 20 km or part thereof = 1 additional day.
Relevant date: Day 1 expires at 12:00 midnight of the day immediately following the date of generation.
Validity starts when first entry is made in Part B.

flow.title: Validity & Cancellation Timeline
steps: Generate E-Way Bill on Portal
Optional cancellation within 24 hours (unless verified)
15 days window to update Part-B (if pending)
Validity starts upon first Part-B entry
Each day expires at midnight of following day

topics.example: E-Way Bill generated at 10:00 AM on 1st April for 150 km normal cargo. It is valid till 12:00 Midnight of 2nd April (1 day from midnight following generation).
remember: Cancellation window: 24 hours from generation.
Normal cargo: 1 day per 200 km.
ODC cargo: 1 day per 20 km.
Day count expires at midnight of the next day.
mistakes: Attempting to edit an E-Way Bill with errors. (Editing is not allowed; only cancellation within 24 hours and regeneration).

quiz.q: Within what time limit can an E-Way Bill be cancelled after generation?
quiz.why: Rule 138(9) allows cancellation of E-Way Bill electronically within 24 hours of generation.

quiz.q: What is the validity period of an E-Way Bill for a distance of 350 km for normal cargo?
quiz.why: Up to 200 km = 1 day, and for the remaining 150 km (part of 200 km) = 1 additional day. Total = 2 days.

topics.title: Extension of Validity & Acceptance / Rejection Rules
explain: Extension by Transporter: Transporter can extend validity in exceptional circumstances (breakdown, natural calamity, transshipment delay).
Extension request must be submitted within 8 hours from the time of EWB expiry after updating Part B.
Extension by Commissioner: Commissioner may extend validity for specified categories of goods by notification.
Acceptance/Rejection: Generated E-Way Bill details are made available to registered recipient/supplier on portal.
Deemed Acceptance: If recipient/supplier does not accept or reject within 72 hours OR time of delivery of goods (whichever is earlier), it is deemed accepted.
Inter-State Validity: E-Way Bill generated in one State/UT is valid in all other States/UTs across India.

flow.title: Extension & Deemed Acceptance Mechanism
steps: Vehicle delayed due to breakdown/calamity
Apply for validity extension within 8 hours of expiry
Details notified to recipient on portal
Recipient accepts/rejects on portal
Deemed accepted if no action within 72 hrs / delivery

topics.example: A truck carrying goods gets stuck in a flash flood. The transporter updates Part B and extends EWB validity on the portal within 8 hours after its scheduled expiry.
remember: Extension window: Within 8 hours from time of expiry.
Deemed acceptance limit: 72 hours or time of delivery, whichever is earlier.
EWB generated in any State is valid nationwide.
mistakes: Believing deemed acceptance occurs after 7 days instead of 72 hours.

quiz.q: Within what time frame after expiry can a transporter extend the validity of an E-Way Bill?
quiz.why: Transporter can extend validity of E-Way Bill within 8 hours from the time of its expiry in exceptional circumstances.

quiz.q: When is an E-Way Bill deemed to be accepted by the recipient?
o: Within 72 hours of details being available or delivery of goods, whichever is earlier
quiz.why: Rule 138(12) specifies deemed acceptance if not communicated within 72 hours or delivery of goods, whichever is earlier.

topics.title: Situations Exempted from E-Way Bill Generation
explain: No E-Way Bill is required for specified goods: LPG (household/NDEC), Kerosene under PDS, Postal baggage, Chapter 71 (precious metals, pearls, jewellery except imitation jewellery 7117), Currency, Used personal/household effects, Coral.
Non-motorised conveyance transport does not require E-Way Bill.
Customs Movement: Transport from port/airport/ICD/CFS under customs bond or supervision.
Exempt Goods: Transport of goods exempt from tax (other than de-oiled cake).
Non-GST Goods: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption, petroleum crude, motor spirit (petrol), diesel, natural gas, ATF.
Schedule III items (treated as no supply).
Empty cargo containers & empty LPG cylinders moved for reasons other than supply.
Goods moved up to 20 km to a weighbridge for weighment and back, accompanied by a delivery challan.

flow.title: Exemption Verification Process
steps: Check type of goods being transported
Check if goods are exempt or non-GST items
Check mode (motorised vs non-motorised)
Check purpose (e.g., weighbridge ≤ 20 km)
If exempt condition met, skip EWB generation

topics.example: Talli Lal transports alcoholic liquor for human consumption worth ₹ 1,50,000. Since liquor is outside GST, no E-Way Bill is required.
remember: Jewellery/Precious metals (Chapter 71) exempt EXCEPT Imitation Jewellery (7117).
Weighbridge transport exempt up to 20 km with delivery challan.
Non-motorised transport is totally exempt.
mistakes: Assuming imitation jewellery is exempt from E-Way Bill. (Imitation jewellery under 7117 REQUIRES E-Way Bill).

quiz.q: Which of the following items requires an E-Way Bill?
o: Liquefied petroleum gas for household use
quiz.why: Chapter 71 items are exempt from E-Way Bill EXCEPT imitation jewellery under HSN 7117.

quiz.q: What is the maximum distance allowed for transporting goods to a weighbridge without an E-Way Bill?
quiz.why: Rule 138(14)(n) exempts movement up to 20 km from business premises to weighbridge and back, accompanied by a delivery challan.

topics.title: Inspection, Verification, Detention & Documents to Carry
explain: Documents to Carry [Rule 138A]: Invoice / Bill of Supply / Delivery Challan AND copy of E-Way Bill (physical/electronic or RFID mapped).
For e-invoices, QR code with embedded IRN can be produced electronically in lieu of physical tax invoice.
If E-Way Bill is not required under rules, person in charge must carry tax invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan [Rule 55A].
Verification [Rule 138B]: Proper officer can intercept conveyance to verify EWB in physical/electronic form or via RFID readers.
Inspection Report [Rule 138C]: Online summary report in Part A within 24 hours of inspection; final report in Part B within 3 days (extendable by 3 days).
No repeat physical verification in same State unless specific evasion info is received.
Detention Upload [Rule 138D]: If vehicle is detained for > 30 minutes, transporter can upload information on common portal.

flow.title: Inspection & Reporting Sequence
steps: Officer intercepts conveyance in transit
Inspects documents / QR Code / RFID / E-Way Bill
Submits online Part-A summary report within 24 hours
Submits online Part-B final report within 3 days
Transporter logs detention if held > 30 minutes

topics.example: A truck is intercepted by GST officers. The officer uploads an online summary report within 24 hours and the final inspection report within 3 days on the portal.
remember: Part A Inspection Report = Within 24 hours.
Part B Inspection Report = Within 3 days (extension max 3 days).
Detention logging threshold = Exceeding 30 minutes.
mistakes: Thinking physical verification can be conducted repeatedly during the same transit without fresh evasion info.

quiz.q: Within what time must the proper officer submit the final online inspection report in Part B after inspecting goods in transit?
quiz.why: Rule 138C requires the summary report in Part A within 24 hours and final report in Part B within 3 days.

quiz.q: If a vehicle is detained by tax officers beyond what duration can the transporter upload detention info on the portal?
quiz.why: Rule 138D allows transporters to upload detention information if vehicle interception/detention exceeds 30 minutes.

topics.title: Blocking of E-Way Bill Generation Facility
explain: Blocking means disabling a GSTIN from generating E-Way Bills for OUTWARD movement of goods.
Composition Taxpayer: Blocked if statement for self-assessed tax (CMP-08) is not furnished for 2 consecutive quarters.
Regular Taxpayer: Blocked if returns (GSTR-3B) are not furnished for 2 consecutive tax periods.
GSTR-1 Non-filers: Blocked if GSTR-1 is not furnished for 2 months / quarters.
Suspended Registration: Blocked if GST registration is suspended under Rule 21A.
Blocking applies ONLY to defaulting SUPPLIER GSTIN. Suspended GSTIN can still receive goods (as recipient) or transport goods.
Unblocking: Jurisdictional Commissioner can unblock facility upon application showing sufficient cause.

flow.title: E-Way Bill Blocking & Unblocking Workflow
steps: Taxpayer fails to file returns for 2 consecutive periods
System automatically blocks GSTIN for outward EWB
Defaulting GSTIN cannot generate EWB as Supplier
Taxpayer files pending returns or applies to Commissioner
Commissioner unblocks E-Way Bill facility

topics.example: Mr. A (Delhi) hasn't filed GSTR-3B for 2 months. He cannot generate E-Way Bill as a supplier. However, Mr. B (Haryana) can generate an E-Way Bill to supply goods to Mr. A since Mr. B is regular.
remember: Composition: 2 consecutive quarters non-filing.
Regular: 2 consecutive tax periods GSTR-3B / 2 months GSTR-1 non-filing.
Blocking restricts generation as SUPPLIER, not as Recipient/Transporter.
mistakes: Assuming a blocked taxpayer cannot receive goods from other compliant suppliers.

quiz.q: A regular scheme taxpayer will be blocked from generating E-Way Bills if they fail to file GSTR-3B for how long?
quiz.why: Rule 138E(ii) blocks EWB generation facility if a regular taxpayer does not furnish returns for 2 consecutive tax periods.

quiz.q: Does the blocking of E-Way Bill facility prevent a defaulting buyer from receiving goods?
o: Yes, all movements are completely stopped
No, blocking only applies to outward supplies as a supplier
Yes, recipient GSTIN is cancelled automatically
quiz.why: Blocking applies only to the defaulting supplier's GSTIN for outward movement; a non-defaulting supplier can still generate EWB to deliver goods to them.
